newsitem.title: USA: ADP to divest part of auto parts business.
newsitem.headline: ADP to divest part of auto parts business.

text.p: Automatic Data Processing Inc said Wednesday it will divest certain assets of its auto parts service business under a settlement with the staff of the Federal Trade Commission.
The assets to be divested generate $15 million in annual revenues and were acquired in April 1995 from AutoInfo Inc, ADP said in a statement.
ADP's auto parts service business services the U.S. and Canadian automotive salvage yard industry.
ADP said the disposition of the assets will not have a material impact on its financial results.
The settlement was agreed to because it was not economically possible to justify an extended, expensive legal battle, ADP said.
Assets to be divested include the Checkmate management system, Orion parts locating network, Compass Voice Line system, and the former AutoInfo Interchange.

Not included in the divestiture are the Hollander line of products and services, including the Hollander Yard Management System, Hollander Interchange, Electronic Data Exchange Network (EDEN), and the Hollander Interchange manuals, the company said.
